study.question: Does the replicated rank96-to88 click-AUC loss partly arise from lower fresh-context initialization energy, and can matching rank96 energy recover rank88 utility with fewer parameters and measured prediction cost?
study.hypothesis: Observation: g2-r0063-context_gauge96_balanced reproduced AUC0.6675003890552496; balanced rank88 reproduced0.6671251297972951, a loss0.0003752592579545. Rank88 output-heavy gave0.6670903354381091 and did not rescue it; rank96 output-heavy also fell to0.667086629350575. These are repeated same-seed executions, not independent seed support. Removing8 directions also lowers initial squared Frobenius norm. Hypothesis: a recoverable part of this loss is caused by product-scale-dependent optimization/normalization and shared upstream gradients, rather than rank ceiling alone. Gauge controls held the real-arithmetic initial product fixed and therefore did not isolate its norm. Counterevidence: g2-r0056-joint_energy_norm35 (0.66682759997943) was worse than raw35 (0.6669746715660667); broad energy restoration is not established. The present bounded symmetric rank-by-energy contrast tests transfer at88/96, without assuming it. Simple embedding/scorer reductions and shared projection replacement failed earlier; evaluation folding preserved AUC without reliable speed gain, so capacity, information flow and runtime must remain separate claims.
